title: Technical Spec
description: A technical spec (TECH): one coherent cross-cutting convention (style, structure, security, traceability, documentation), with its individual rules captured as acceptance criteria. Applies repo-wide.

title.description: Short human-readable summary of the spec.

description.description: Narrative: rationale for the rule and what it protects against.

include_for_all_repos.description: When true, `spex init` adds this spec to every workspace repository's tech-specs list, including spex itself. Defaults to false.

include_for_spex.description: Overrides spex-repo inclusion when present. When omitted, the spex repository follows `include_for_all_repos`; set explicitly to add or exclude this spec for the spex repository.

readonly.description: When true, this is a global spex framework spec that can be changed only upstream. Consumers must not edit it locally; updates arrive by upgrading spex. Defaults to false.

acceptance_criteria.description: Verifiable acceptance criteria. Order by commitment level: MUST, then MUST NOT, then SHOULD, then SHOULD NOT, then MAY.

items.description: A single verifiable acceptance criterion, provable by automated checks or AI. Starts with a commitment level.

checks.description: Automated checks that verify the spec's acceptance criteria.

examples.description: Named illustrative snippets showing the spec applied in context — placement and usage that prose cannot carry. Keys are short labels (e.g. `template`, `contract`, `avoid`, `prefer`); values are code or text blocks.

examples.title: Secret protection
examples.description: Hardcoded credentials, API keys, and tokens in the repository are a common source of security breaches. Secrets must be provided through environment variables or a dedicated secrets manager so they are never committed to version control.
acceptance_criteria: MUST NOT commit API keys, passwords, or tokens to the repository
MUST load secrets from environment variables or a secrets manager at runtime
SHOULD fail CI when a secret-scanning check detects credentials in a diff

checks.name: hardcoded-secrets
checks.description: Detect potential hardcoded secrets in source
